chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Ali al-Sa'igh, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Do I accept the work (wage) and then give it to the boys who work with me for two-thirds?' He said: 'That is not suitable unless you work with them in it.' I said: 'I pay it to them.' He said: 'That is work, so there is no harm.'

key_terms.أُذِيبُهُ: I pay it (from the verb zabba, to pay out)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a foreman to distribute wages to workers under his supervision according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between two modes of labor management: direct participation in the work (*mu'ashara*) versus a managerial or entrepreneurial role where one oversees and pays others. The Imam validates the latter as a legitimate form of 'work' (*amal*), establishing the permissibility of profit-sharing or wage-distribution models in Islamic commercial jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia fiqh in accommodating diverse economic arrangements provided they are grounded in clear contractual intent and active engagement, whether physical or supervisory.
